summary.text: Andrew Garbarino is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 2nd Congressional District. A Long Island native and attorney, he served in the New York State Assembly from 2013 to 2020 before being elected to Congress in 2020. He chairs the House Homeland Security Committee and also serves on the Financial Services and Ethics committees.

paragraphs.text: Andrew Garbarino was born in Sayville, New York, in 1984, raised there, and graduated from Sayville High School.
He earned a B.A. in history and classical humanities from George Washington University and a J.D. from Hofstra University.
After law school he worked at his family's law firm in Sayville.
Garbarino represented the 7th District in the New York State Assembly from 2013 to 2020, winning the seat in 2012 and re-election in 2014, 2016 and 2018.

According to his campaign website's text republished by Ballotpedia, he voted against the 2019 bail-reform bill and cosponsored a bill making it a felony to intentionally interfere with a police or peace officer performing official duties.

In 2020 he won the Republican primary for NY-2 after Rep. Peter King announced his retirement, then defeated Democrat Jackie Gordon in the general election; he took office January 3, 2021, and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Garbarino's committee assignments in the 119th Congress are Homeland Security (Chairman), Financial Services (Vice Chairman of the Capital Markets Subcommittee) and Ethics; he became Homeland Security chair in July 2025 after the resignation of Mark Green.

His House biography says he co-chairs the Congressional SALT Caucus and led negotiations to raise the State and Local Tax deduction cap to $40,000, and that he has worked on funding for the World Trade Center Health Program.
He is a member of the Sayville Rotary Club and Knights of Columbus, and his official biography describes him as a lifelong Long Islander.
